c2.label: First look
c2.why: No test yet separates more sharks from more listening stations, so it is described rather than tested.

c7.label: First look
c7.why: Too few recent bites to test.

c9.label: First look
c9.why: The records can describe the wounds but not the time to stop bleeding.

c20.label: First look
c20.why: Without past gear locations it can only describe counts.

c22.label: First look
c22.why: The island coasts never cool below 19°C, so they can't test the line.

c30.label: First look
c30.why: First look at public tagging data for young white sharks.

c1.label: Early result: leans toward it
c1.why: Share of catch stands in for catch per net or drumline, which isn't published, so it can reach "leans toward it" at most.

c1.label: Early result: no clear link
c1.why: A study that allowed for fishing effort (Banaghan et al. 2025) found no clear rise in southern catch rates.

c3.label: Early result: leans toward it
c3.why: Most climate models take the line to Eden but not past the border the claim names.

c4.label: Early result: leans toward it
c4.why: Satellite chlorophyll, a stand-in for baitfish, leans the predicted way.

c4.label: First look
c4.why: The test used satellite chlorophyll and did not measure when baitfish run, so it describes the data rather than testing the claim.

c5.label: Ruled out
c5.why: Its own rules-out condition was met: Queensland's white shark catches didn't grow with the whales.

c6.label: Early result: leans toward it
c6.why: The main rain test passed, but river flow didn't agree and bite dates are monthly.

c16.label: Early result: leans toward it
c16.why: Holding the listening stations fixed weakened the trend.

c18.label: Early result: leans toward it
c18.why: People living on the coast stand in for people on the beach.

c19.label: Early result: leans toward it
c19.why: The day-by-day heatwave check didn't clearly agree with the monthly test.

c21.label: Early result: leans toward it
c21.why: Bites by species stand in for catches by hour.

c21.label: First look
c21.why: The night result rested on six bites, and bites stand in for catches by hour, so it describes the data rather than testing the claim.

c23.label: Early result: points the other way
c23.why: A clear shift in the opposite direction to the claim.

c24.label: Ruled out
c24.why: The 95% range rules out a moon effect worth acting on.

c25.label: Early result: supports it
c25.why: Tested on its own measure on two coasts, in the predicted direction.

c25.label: Early result: leans toward it
c25.why: Retested with daily sea temperature and tag thermometers. Off the US, 10.6% of bull shark days were below 19°C, above the 5% set before the test; young bull sharks overwinter in colder rivers.

c26.label: Early result: no clear link
c26.why: Comparing like with like removed the link.

c28.label: Early result: no clear link
c28.why: Both tests came out where chance puts them.

c29.label: Early result: points the other way
c29.why: An exact two-sided test shows fewer incidents than chance after strong upwelling.

c29.label: Early result: leans the other way
c29.why: Strong upwelling also keeps people out of the water, so fewer incidents can't show fewer sharks.
